- File: scripts/orchestrate_lib.py
  Line or code reference: lines 1629-1635 (_parse_iso8601_to_epoch)
  Problem: The `return None` inside the `except` block now has 3 tabs of indentation instead of the correct 2 tabs. In Python, the `except` body must be indented exactly one level deeper than the `except` keyword. The extra tab makes it a syntactically valid nested block (Python permits arbitrary additional indentation on continuation), but it is inconsistent with every other except-handler in the file and visually misleading.
  Why it fails at runtime: It does not cause a runtime failure — Python accepts the extra whitespace — but it is a style regression that will trip up readers and any automated style checkers expecting consistent 2-tab indented except bodies. The change is a merge-resolution artifact (visible in the last_commit_stat as touching orchestrate_lib.py with indentation churn).
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 12308-12323 (headPushedAt extraction block)
  Problem: The same merge-resolution indentation issue appears here. Lines that previously used 6-space indentation (`      fi`, `      [ -n ...`, etc.) now use a hard tab (`\t      fi`, `\t      [ -n ...`, etc.). The mixed tabs-and-spaces indentation inside this `if` block is inconsistent with the surrounding code in the poller, which uses tabs-only for indentation.
  Why it fails at runtime: Bash is whitespace-agnostic for its own syntax, so this does not cause a runtime failure. But it is a style regression introduced by merge conflict resolution that violates the repo's tab-indentation convention (agents.md §11) and will be flagged by editors/linters.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
